security_audit.summary: All 12 static findings were reviewed against SKILL.md. The Markdown backtick detections are formatting false positives, and the API key detections are placeholder credentials in examples. One semantic issue remains: the webhook sample should show authentication, authorization, and input validation before processing customer data.

remediation.issue: Webhook example accepts provider callbacks without visible verification.
remediation.suggestion: Show webhook signature validation, request schema validation, and authorization checks before calling business functions or saving transcripts.

remediation.issue: API key examples use literal placeholder assignments.
remediation.suggestion: Replace hardcoded placeholder assignments with environment variable or secret manager examples, and state that keys must never be committed.

remediation.issue: Transcript handling is shown without privacy controls.
remediation.suggestion: Add guidance for consent, retention limits, redaction, and secure storage when saving voice transcripts.

semantic_findings.title: Webhook Sample Omits Authentication Checks
semantic_findings.description: The Vapi webhook example processes incoming request data, performs an order lookup, and saves call transcripts without showing signature verification, caller authorization, or input validation. Developers could copy this pattern into production and expose customer data to forged webhook requests.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The sample clearly handles webhook data and transcript storage without any visible verification step. It is documentation rather than runnable package code, so confidence is high enough to flag but not critical.

content.value_statement: Voice teams need fast, reliable guidance across many speech providers. This skill helps design low-latency agents, transcription pipelines, synthesis flows, and real-time infrastructure.
actual_capabilities: Explains when to use OpenAI Realtime API for integrated voice-to-voice agents.
Shows Vapi patterns for hosted phone and web voice agents.
Describes Deepgram streaming transcription settings and event handling.
Describes ElevenLabs streaming synthesis for low-latency audio output.
Covers WebRTC and LiveKit as real-time infrastructure choices.
Identifies latency anti-patterns such as non-streaming pipelines and missed interruptions.
limitations: Examples are illustrative snippets, not a complete runnable application.
Provider APIs, model names, and pricing can change after publication.
Users must supply their own provider accounts, keys, audio devices, and deployment infrastructure.
Production systems still need security review, privacy controls, monitoring, and load testing.

use_cases.title: Prototype a Support Voice Agent
use_cases.description: Plan a first working voice assistant with provider choices, call flow, and latency targets.

use_cases.title: Design a Phone Automation Stack
use_cases.description: Select Vapi, telephony, transcription, synthesis, and webhook patterns for inbound or outbound calls.

use_cases.title: Optimize a Streaming Speech Pipeline
use_cases.description: Improve STT, LLM, and TTS streaming choices to reduce perceived response delay.

prompt_templates.title: Plan My First Voice Agent
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for a simple agent.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me design a basic voice AI agent for [use case]. Include provider options, call flow, latency goals, and main implementation steps.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Voice Providers
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare OpenAI Realtime API, Vapi, Deepgram, ElevenLabs, and LiveKit for [project]. Recommend a stack based on latency, quality, control, and cost.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Streaming Pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a streaming STT to LLM to TTS architecture for [application]. Include interruption handling, partial results, buffering, and failure paths.

prompt_templates.title: Review Production Readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my voice AI architecture for production readiness. Focus on latency budget, provider failures, webhook security, transcript privacy, observability, and scaling risks.

output_examples.input: Design an inbound support voice agent using Vapi and Deepgram.
output_examples.output: Recommended architecture: Vapi manages phone calls and assistant routing. Deepgram provides streaming transcripts. Webhooks should verify signatures before looking up orders or storing transcripts.

output_examples.input: Improve latency in a custom STT, LLM, and TTS pipeline.
output: Enable interim transcription results so the assistant can start reasoning before final speech ends.
Stream model output and begin synthesis once a stable sentence fragment is available.
Support barge-in by stopping playback and clearing queued audio when user speech resumes.

output_examples.input: Choose between OpenAI Realtime API and separate STT/TTS providers.
output_examples.output: Use OpenAI Realtime API when simplicity and integrated voice interaction matter most. Use separate providers when you need specialized transcription, custom voices, or deeper pipeline control.

best_practices: Stream audio, transcripts, model output, and synthesis wherever the provider supports it.
Define a latency budget before choosing providers or infrastructure.
Implement interruption handling so users can speak over the assistant naturally.
anti_patterns: Building a non-streaming pipeline that waits for each stage to finish before starting the next.
Ignoring voice activity detection and forcing users to wait through long responses.
Choosing one provider for every stage without checking quality, latency, cost, or resilience.

faq.question: Does this skill build a complete voice application?
faq.answer: No. It provides architecture guidance, provider patterns, and implementation direction for building your own application.

faq.question: Which providers does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers OpenAI Realtime API, Vapi, Deepgram, ElevenLabs, LiveKit, and WebRTC concepts.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, or Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it include production security guidance?
faq.answer: It includes some architecture guidance, but production systems need additional review for webhooks, secrets, privacy, and monitoring.

faq.question: Is it only for phone agents?
faq.answer: No. It covers phone agents, web voice agents, custom streaming pipelines, and real-time audio infrastructure.

faq.question: What knowledge should users have first?
faq.answer: Users should understand Python or Node.js basics, API credentials, audio formats, and provider account setup.
